Reproducing Guo et al. (2017) from dandiset 000009¶

Paper. Guo ZV, Inagaki HK, Daie K, Druckmann S, Gerfen CR, Svoboda K (2017). Maintenance of persistent activity in a frontal thalamocortical loop. Nature 545, 181-186. doi:10.1038/nature22324. The claims file (claims/000009/10.1038-nature22324.yaml) was written from the HHMI author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC6431254): main text, Methods and the legends of Figures 1 to 6 and Extended Data Figures 1 to 10; the Supplementary Information and Supplementary Tables were not in the text read.

Dandiset. DANDI:000009, version 0.220126.1903. The paper cites no DANDI version (it names a CRCNS deposit, doi:10.6080/K03F4MH2). This is the only published version; the draft lists the same 173 assets and size, so the most recent published version is pinned.

What the dandiset holds. 137 silicon-probe sessions (ALM, thalamus, SNr) with trial tables, spike times, mean waveforms and unit positions, and 36 whole-cell recordings of ALM neurons during thalamus, M1 or contralateral ALM photoinhibition, from 31 mice. Behaviour-only sessions, the muscimol experiments, the weak photoinhibition of Fig. 5, non-behaving and M1 whole-cell recordings and the anatomy are not in it.

Questions asked and answered (questions/000009.yaml; the answers of 2026-10-20 are written into the claims file, and this notebook follows them):

  1. Unit classes. P1 (width computed on the deposited waveforms) is the Methods' rule; P2 (the files' cell_type label) stays a reading, as the paper does not say how the label was made. For the thalamic claims of Fig. 2 and 6, all units regardless of width is a further reading (P3, convention C), added here to fig2f-vmval-selectivity, fig6c-vmval-reduced, fig6b, fig6c-unmodulated, fig6d (its reading u2), vm1-photoinhibition-no-effect, fig6e and selectivity-time-course.
  2. The PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions with thalamic photostimulation are not part of Fig. 3, which uses VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice at 10 mW; they stay a variant.
  3. ALM photoinhibition is the 1.5 mW condition; trials at 0.75 or 0.79 mW are outside it, and all powers pooled is a variant.
  4. The whole-cell photostimulus onset has two readings, E (1.3 s after pole_in_time) and M (0.1 s after pole_out_time); placing it from the Vm change is not a reading. The answer assumed the files hold no laser time; they do (an OptogeneticSeries at 20 kHz, found after the first verification), so the onset of that trace is shown as a third reading, L, and a new question asks whether it should be used (question 7 below). The outcomes of the four whole-cell claims are the same under M and under L.
  5. The paper does not say which deposited condition is vM1; ALM is compared at 1.5 mW, matched power is a variant. The claim stays blocked on the site.
  6. Selectivity time course: correct control trials (t1) and all correct trials (t2) are both readings.
  7. Asked after the first verification, not yet answered: should the whole-cell photostimulus onset be taken from the deposited laser trace (reading L)? Under L the onset latency of wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization can be measured; no outcome depends on the answer.

Changes after the first verification: within a trial the extracellular files store spikes only to about 4.8 s after pole onset, so a window that ends later is now counted as missing for that trial (it had been counted with the spikes it held); SNr reading P2 is now the 'Narrow width spiking' label (146 units), as convention C says; the whole-cell laser trace is read; and checks were added for the onset rule, the VGAT delay lengths and the spike-threshold kink.

Changes after the second verification: no outcome changed in that round. The verifier found that nine claims were given partially reproduced under criteria with no partial clause; a section before the Summary counts the readings that meet each whole criterion (none does), and a change to not reproduced was proposed for each. Some sentences were corrected.

Changes after the third verification: the verifier agreed with all nine proposed changes, so alm-unit-classes, fig2e-alm-selectivity, thalamus-unit-classes, fig2f-vmval-selectivity, fig3f-thalamus-silenced, wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization, wc-m1-small-effect, fig6d-localized and snr-photoinhibition are now not reproduced.

# LOAD-CELL
import time
import warnings
from collections import Counter

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import loop

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
assets = loop.list_assets()
sessions = loop.load_all_ecephys(assets)
cells = loop.load_all_wholecell(assets)
units = loop.unit_table(sessions)
units["vmval_d"] = loop.vmval_distance(units)
print(f"dandiset {loop.DANDISET_ID} version {loop.DANDISET_VERSION}: {len(assets)} assets; loaded "
      f"{len(sessions)} extracellular sessions ({len(units)} units) and {len(cells)} whole-cell recordings "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

The dandiset holds 137 extracellular sessions and 36 whole-cell recordings from 31 mice, as the archive says. ALM: 47 sessions from 10 mice with 966 units, against 57 sessions and 1214 units in the paper (10 mice). Thalamus: 72 sessions with 789 units, against 73 and 790. SNr: 18 sessions with 181 units, against 23 sessions and 227 units, of which the paper keeps 181 as putative GABAergic. The whole-cell recordings are 16 ALM cells during thalamus photoinhibition (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP), 11 during M1 and 9 during contralateral ALM photoinhibition (PV-Cre x Ai32), the n of Fig. 3g and 4. Not in the dandiset: behaviour-only sessions, the muscimol experiments, the weak (0.5 mW) thalamus photoinhibition of Fig. 5, non-behaving whole-cell recordings (Extended Data Fig. 5c-h, 6c), M1 whole-cell recordings, and the anatomy.

What the files hold that the paper does not describe, or describes differently:

  • The 9 thalamic sessions of two Ai35D x GAD2_Cre mice carry no photostimulus in any trial (every period 'N/A', power 0), yet their 84 units equal the 26 + 41 + 17 Gad2-IRES-Cre optrode units of Extended Data Fig. 2c. The paper's Gad2 mice had ChR2 injected in TRN; Ai35D is an Arch line. 12 thalamic sessions of two C57BL6 mice (104 units) have no photostimulus either.
  • 21 ALM sessions of four Ai32 x PV-Cre mice have photostimulation of the thalamus at 10, 22.5 and 45 mW. The paper describes ALM recordings during thalamus photoinhibition in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice only (Fig. 3); the 18 VGAT ALM sessions here use 10 mW.
  • The VGAT thalamic sessions record 2.23 mW where the paper gives 10 mW (Extended Data Fig. 2d), and one of them was photostimulated in the sample epoch.
  • In thalamic sessions of mouse anm00264943, ALM photoinhibition at 0.79 and 1.5 mW is interleaved with photostimulation at galvo position (0.5, 0.5) mm, which is not named. The paper interleaves ALM and vM1 photoinhibition in 3 mice (Extended Data Fig. 8f, g).
  • Trials labelled 'delay' with power 0 (a few per session) are kept apart and used in no analysis.

# Recordings deposited twice: compare trial start times and unit spike counts between every pair.
sig = []
for i, s in enumerate(sessions):
    t = s["trials"]
    sig.append((i, s["meta"]["subject"], tuple(np.round(t.start_time.values[:20], 3)),
                set(zip(s["units"].n_spikes, np.round(s["units"].first_spike, 4)))))
pairs = []
for a in range(len(sig)):
    for b in range(a + 1, len(sig)):
        same_trials = sig[a][2] == sig[b][2]
        shared_units = len(sig[a][3] & sig[b][3])
        if same_trials or shared_units:
            pairs.append((sessions[a]["meta"]["path"], sessions[b]["meta"]["path"], same_trials, shared_units))
print("Extracellular session pairs sharing trial start times or units (spike count and first spike):", pairs if pairs else "none")
wsig = [(c["meta"]["path"], c["meta"]["n_samples"], c["meta"]["n_spikes"], round(c["meta"]["vm_range"][0], 3)) for c in cells]
dup = [(a[0], b[0]) for i, a in enumerate(wsig) for b in wsig[i + 1:] if a[1:] == b[1:]]
print("Whole-cell pairs with equal length, spike count and minimum Vm:", dup if dup else "none")
starts = pd.DataFrame([(c["meta"]["subject"], c["meta"]["cell"], c["trials"].start_time.min(), c["trials"].stop_time.max())
                       for c in cells], columns=["subject", "cell", "first", "last"])
print("Whole-cell cells per mouse:", starts.groupby("subject").cell.apply(list).to_dict())

No session or whole-cell recording is deposited twice: no two sessions share trial start times or any unit. Each whole-cell file holds one cell; cells of one mouse are counted as separate cells, as in the paper. A unit is never treated as the same across sessions here.

The deposited mean waveforms are short: 29 samples at 25 kHz (1.16 ms) in thalamus and SNr, and the trough sits at sample 15 to 19, so a trough-to-peak interval longer than 0.36 to 0.52 ms cannot be measured in many units. The peak after the trough is the last sample in 78% of ALM units labelled 'Wide width spiking'. Widths computed from these waveforms are therefore lower bounds for wide units, and the classes the Methods define by width (> 0.6 ms in ALM, > 0.5 ms in thalamus) cannot be recovered from them. The files' own cell_type labels ('Wide width spiking', 'Narrow width spiking', 'Cannot be determined') separate the units cleanly by computed width (narrow up to 0.32 ms in ALM, wide from 0.44 ms) and are shown below as the second reading (P2) of every unit class; reading P1 applies the Methods' thresholds to the computed widths.

Coordinates: unit_x is medio-lateral (positive), unit_y dorso-ventral (negative, mm), unit_z antero-posterior; thalamic units lie between AP -1.2 and -2.1 mm, inside the "bregma -1 to -2 mm" of the Methods, and ALM units at AP 2.5 to 3.0. Two inconsistencies: every electrode group, also in thalamus and SNr, carries the ALM coordinates (AP 2.5, ML -1.5, DV 0); and the SNr units of mouse anm00261336 are at AP -1.56 mm, where SNr is not (the other two SNr mice are at AP -3.6 to -4.2). Photostimulus sites give ML negative for the left hemisphere, units give it positive. The thalamic fibre site is the same nominal coordinate (AP -1.5, ML 0.9, DV -4.1) in all 29 sessions.

Spikes are stored only in part of each trial and for part of each session. Within a trial, spikes run from the trial start (0.57 s before pole onset) to about 4.8 s after pole onset: the summed rate 5.5 to 8 s after pole onset is 1.4% of that 2 to 4.5 s after it, although trials last about 9 s. The end is fixed to pole onset, not to the go cue (next table), so in trials with a long delay the response epoch, and in a few the delay epoch, runs past the stored spikes. Each trial's stored span is taken to end at the last spike of any unit of the session in it, and a window that ends later is counted as missing for that trial. Across a session, most units hold spikes over only some of its trials (median 70%), and the files give no observation interval per unit. A unit's trials are therefore taken to run from the trial holding its first spike to the trial holding its last; trials outside count as missing, not as zero spikes. This is a standard choice recorded as a deviation.

Trial types are 'lick left', 'lick right' and 'non-performing'; contra trials are taken as 'lick right' (left hemisphere, Fig. 1a). 5375 extracellular rows have no outcome ('N/A', type 'non-performing'); 5369 of them have no pole times and are dropped, and the other 6 enter no analysis. In the extracellular files the delay (go cue minus 1.3 s after pole onset) is 1.3 s in 81% of trials and never 1.2 s; the rest are longer (up to 4.4 s at the 99th percentile). pole_out_time is 1.3 s after pole_in_time. Trials last about 9 s. In the whole-cell files pole_out_time is 1.4 s after pole_in_time and the go cue 2.6 s after it. One whole-cell trial table is not in time order and has a row whose start time (774 s) does not contain its pole onset (12 s). The whole-cell trial tables leave every photostimulus column empty; stim_present marks 30 to 50% of trials, the "25-50%" of the Methods for Fig. 3g and 4, and is read as the photostimulus flag (its effect is shown below).

The end of the stored spikes is fixed to pole onset: its median is 4.81 to 4.84 s after pole onset whatever the delay, so it falls 2.2 s after the go cue in trials with a 1.3 s delay and before the go cue in trials with a delay above 3 s (table). Before this correction, such windows were counted with the spikes they held, which biased their counts low. Every correct or incorrect trial has a 1.3 s delay; the longer delays occur only in lick-early and no-response trials, which no analysis uses. The correction therefore touches only the kept trials whose stored spikes end early: 221 of 8991 in ALM, 173 of 14997 in thalamus and 19 of 3573 in SNr for R1.

# Clock check, extracellular: the photostimulus effect must start at the onset the trial table gives
# (1.3 s after pole onset), and trial types must be decodable with true but not shifted labels.
t_ms = loop.psth_time_ms()
checks = [("VGAT thalamus, thalamus photostim.", (units.genotype == "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP") & (units.region == "Thalamus"), ["Thalamus:delay:2.23"]),
          ("VGAT ALM, thalamus photostim.", (units.genotype == "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP") & (units.region == "ALM"), ["Thalamus:delay:10"]),
          ("PV ALM, thalamus photostim. 10 mW", (units.genotype == "Ai32 x PV-Cre") & (units.region == "ALM") & (units.ogen_site == "Thalamus"), ["Thalamus:delay:10"]),
          ("PV thalamus, ALM photoinh. 1.5 mW", (units.genotype == "Ai32 x PV-Cre") & (units.region == "Thalamus"), ["ALM:delay:1.5"]),
          ("PV SNr, ALM photoinh. 1.5 mW", units.region == "SNr", ["ALM:delay:1.5"]),
          ("PV ALM, ALM photoinh. 1.5 mW", (units.genotype == "Ai32 x PV-Cre") & (units.region == "ALM") & (units.ogen_site == "ALM"), ["ALM:delay:1.5"])]
rows = []
for name, sel, st in checks:
    c, p = loop.population_psth(sessions, units[sel], st)
    mc, mp = np.nanmean(c, 0), np.nanmean(p, 0)
    row = {"group": name, "units": int(sel.sum())}
    for lo in (-50, -20, -10, 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, 100):
        k = (t_ms >= lo) & (t_ms < lo + 5 if lo >= 0 else t_ms < lo + 10 if lo == -20 or lo == -10 else t_ms < lo + 30)
        row[f"{lo}"] = round(mp[k].mean() / mc[k].mean(), 2)
    rows.append(row)
print("Population rate under photostimulus / control, in windows starting at the given ms after the onset"
      " (5 ms windows from 0 on; -50 is -50 to -20, -20 and -10 are 10 ms):")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

dec = []
for i, s in enumerate(sessions):
    t = s["trials"]
    m = (t.response == "correct").values & (t.stim == "none").values
    y = t.contra.values[m]
    y_shift = np.roll(t.contra.values, 1)[m]
    c = s["counts"]["delay"][:, m]
    true = np.mean([loop.ttest(u[y], u[~y], True) < 0.05 for u in c])
    shift = np.mean([loop.ttest(u[y_shift], u[~y_shift], True) < 0.05 for u in c])
    dec.append((s["meta"]["region"], true, shift))
dec = pd.DataFrame(dec, columns=["region", "true", "shifted"])
dec["no_photostim"] = [s["meta"]["ogen_site"] is None for s in sessions]
print("\nFraction of units with delay-epoch contra/ipsi difference (t-test p < 0.05, correct control trials), per session:")
print(dec.groupby("region").agg(sessions=("true", "size"), true_median=("true", "median"), shifted_median=("shifted", "median"),
                                true_gt_shifted=("true", lambda x: int((x > dec.loc[x.index, "shifted"]).sum()))).round(3).to_string())
d0 = dec[dec.no_photostim]
print("Sessions without photostimulus (Gad2, C57BL6):", len(d0), "| true > shifted in", int((d0.true > d0.shifted).sum()),
      "| pooled fraction true", round(d0.true.mean(), 3), "shifted", round(d0.shifted.mean(), 3))

In the extracellular files the photostimulus effect starts where the trial table puts the onset, 1.3 s after pole onset: VGAT thalamic units fall within the first 5 ms, ALM units 10 to 15 ms later, and VM/VAL units under ALM photoinhibition from about 20 ms; before the onset the ratio is near 1. More units distinguish trial types in the delay epoch with true labels than with labels shifted by one trial in 44 of 47 ALM, 14 of 18 SNr and 53 of 72 thalamic sessions, and in 16 of the 21 sessions without a photostimulus (table). The spike times share the clock of the trial tables; this is shown for every group with a photostimulus, and through decoding for the sessions without one (Gad2 and C57BL6 thalamus).

The whole-cell Vm is stored with unit 'mV' and conversion 0.001, but the values are already in mV (minimum -61 to -108 mV, spikes peaking up to +43 mV); applying the conversion, as NWB prescribes, would give values a thousand times too small. The injected current around the photostimulus is 0 nA in every trial. The spike clipping of convention V, computed here from the raw trace, leaves the trace equal to the deposited spike-removed trace (median absolute difference 0 mV in every cell), so the deposited trace is clipped by the same rule. Licks follow the go cue in the lick traces.

The whole-cell files hold the laser trace, as an OptogeneticSeries (stimulus/presentation/photostim_on_*, 20 kHz, unit 'watts' with conversion 0.001, so the values are in mW): a step to 10 mW in the 16 thalamus photoinhibition cells and a sinusoid peaking at 3 mW (1.5 mW mean) in the 20 cortical photoinhibition cells. Before the first verification the loader read only general/optogenetics and this notebook said the files record no laser time; that was wrong. The trace is present in every stim_present trial and in one control trial (cell_21_1, an incorrect trial). The laser starts 1.4725 s after pole_in_time (0.072 s after pole_out_time) in the thalamus cells, 1.474 s after it in 14 cortical cells and 1.4026 s after it (0.002 s after pole_out_time) in the six M1 cells of anm300476. It lasts 1.19 to 1.24 s and ends between 5 ms before and 114 ms after the go cue. In 0 to 8 photostimulus trials per cell it starts more than 20 ms from the cell's median; reading L uses each trial's own onset. Onsets taken at 1% or 20% of the maximum, in place of 5%, differ by 0 ms (step) or 1.0 to 2.5 ms (sinusoid).

Neither onset of the claims file is the laser onset: in the thalamus cells E (1.3 s after pole onset) is 0.17 s before it and M (pole_out_time + 0.1 s, 1.5 s) 28 ms after it. Thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarizes ALM neurons from a median 1.493 s after pole onset (first crossing of 3 SD and 2 mV on 1 ms samples; 1.47 to 1.51 s in 15 of 16 cells), 20 ms after the laser onset by this coarse check. Under E the 20 to 120 ms window (1.32 to 1.42 s) lies before the change in all three groups (table: 0.2 mV for thalamus photoinhibition at 1.32 and 1.40 s). Under M (1.52 to 1.62 s) and L (1.49 to 1.59 s) it lies inside the change. The claims file (answer of 2026-10-20) gives E and M as readings, because it took the files to hold no laser time. Reading L, the onset of the deposited laser trace, is shown here as a third reading, and question 7 asks whether it should be used. Control trials are aligned at the cell's median laser onset. The extracellular files hold no laser trace; there the onset is the delay onset of the trial table, which the clock check above supports.

Selections and readings used by several claims¶

Unit classes (convention C of the claims file): P1 applies the Methods' width thresholds to the trough-to-peak width of the deposited mean waveform (ALM pyramidal > 0.6 ms, thalamic > 0.5 ms, SNr GABAergic < 0.45 ms); P2 uses the files' cell_type label ('Wide width spiking' for ALM pyramidal and thalamic units; 'Narrow width spiking' for SNr GABAergic units, as convention C says; before the first verification this reading took every SNr unit not labelled wide); P3, for the thalamic claims of Fig. 2 and 6 only, takes all thalamic units regardless of width (VM26). VM/VAL: reading L1 (a VM/VAL label in the dataset) does not exist, as every thalamic unit is labelled 'Thalamus'; reading L2 is within 0.4 mm of ML 0.85, DV -4.0 mm in the coronal plane.

Selectivity (convention S) is computed once per reading: trials (control only, or all), response window (R1, R2), t-test (Student, Welch) and outcomes (c1 correct only, c2 correct and incorrect), 16 readings.

In [9]:
alm = units[units.region == "ALM"]
thal = units[units.region == "Thalamus"]
snr = units[units.region == "SNr"]
PYR = {"P1": alm[alm.width_ms > 0.6], "P2": alm[alm.cell_type == "Wide width spiking"]}
THP = {"P1": thal[thal.width_ms > 0.5], "P2": thal[thal.cell_type == "Wide width spiking"]}
GABA = {"P1": snr[snr.width_ms < 0.45], "P2": snr[snr.cell_type == "Narrow width spiking"]}
VMVAL = {p: d[d.vmval_d < 0.4] for p, d in THP.items()}
# Convention C, reading P3: all thalamic units regardless of width, for the thalamic claims of Fig. 2 and 6 only.
VM26 = {**VMVAL, "P3": thal[thal.vmval_d < 0.4]}
SEL_READINGS = [(ts, r, ev, oc) for ts in ("control", "all") for r in ("R1", "R2") for ev in (True, False)
                for oc in (("correct",), ("correct", "incorrect"))]


def sel_key(ts, r, ev, oc):
    return f"{ts}/{r}/{'Student' if ev else 'Welch'}/{'c1' if len(oc) == 1 else 'c2'}"


t0 = time.time()
SEL = {sel_key(*k): loop.selectivity_table(sessions, units, resp=k[1], equal_var=k[2], outcomes=k[3], trials_sel=k[0])
       for k in SEL_READINGS}
print(f"selectivity under {len(SEL)} readings for {len(units)} units in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print("Units per class:", {f"ALM pyramidal {p}": len(d) for p, d in PYR.items()},
      {f"thalamic {p}": len(d) for p, d in THP.items()}, {f"VM/VAL {p}": len(d) for p, d in VM26.items()},
      {f"SNr GABAergic {p}": len(d) for p, d in GABA.items()})

task-performance¶

Mice performed the delayed-response task at 77.6% correct on average, with 10.3% lick-early trials and 1.1% no-response trials.

Readings of the criterion: (a) all trials of all sessions pooled, (b) mean over sessions, (c) control trials only, pooled and per session. Percent correct excludes lick-early and no-response trials; those two are fractions of all task trials. Sessions are every behavioural recording in the dandiset (extracellular sessions and whole-cell recordings), shown also by kind.

In [10]:
prow = []
for s in sessions:
    t = s["trials"]
    prow.append({"kind": "extracellular", "subject": s["meta"]["subject"], "resp": t.response.values, "ctrl": (t.stim == "none").values})
for c in cells:
    t = c["trials"]
    prow.append({"kind": "whole-cell", "subject": c["meta"]["subject"], "resp": t.response.values, "ctrl": ~t.pi.values})


def perf(resp):
    n = len(resp)
    cor, inc = (resp == "correct").sum(), (resp == "incorrect").sum()
    return {"n": n, "correct": 100 * cor / (cor + inc), "early": 100 * (resp == "early lick").sum() / n,
            "noresp": 100 * (resp == "no response").sum() / n}


out = []
for kinds in (("extracellular", "whole-cell"), ("extracellular",), ("whole-cell",)):
    sel = [r for r in prow if r["kind"] in kinds]
    for reading, use_ctrl in (("a/b all trials", False), ("c control trials", True)):
        per = pd.DataFrame([perf(r["resp"][r["ctrl"]] if use_ctrl else r["resp"]) for r in sel])
        pooled = perf(np.concatenate([r["resp"][r["ctrl"]] if use_ctrl else r["resp"] for r in sel]))
        out.append({"files": "+".join(kinds), "trials": reading, "how": "pooled", "sessions": len(sel), "trials_n": pooled["n"],
                    "correct_%": pooled["correct"], "lick_early_%": pooled["early"], "no_response_%": pooled["noresp"]})
        out.append({"files": "+".join(kinds), "trials": reading, "how": "mean over sessions", "sessions": len(sel), "trials_n": int(per.n.sum()),
                    "correct_%": per.correct.mean(), "lick_early_%": per.early.mean(), "no_response_%": per.noresp.mean()})
perf_tab = pd.DataFrame(out)
perf_tab["within_tol"] = ((perf_tab["correct_%"] - 77.6).abs() <= 7.76) & ((perf_tab["lick_early_%"] - 10.3).abs() <= 1.03) & \
    ((perf_tab["no_response_%"] - 1.1).abs() <= 0.11)
print(perf_tab.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("Paper: 77.6 +/- 7.76 % correct, 10.3 +/- 1.03 % lick early, 1.1 +/- 0.11 % no response")
by_mouse = pd.DataFrame([{"subject": r["subject"], **perf(r["resp"])} for r in prow]).groupby("subject")[["correct", "early", "noresp"]].mean()
print("\nPer mouse (mean over its sessions, all trials): correct", by_mouse.correct.round(1).min(), "to", by_mouse.correct.round(1).max(),
      "| lick early", by_mouse.early.round(1).min(), "to", by_mouse.early.round(1).max(), "| no response", by_mouse.noresp.round(2).min(), "to", by_mouse.noresp.round(2).max())

Result: not reproduced. Over all 173 behavioural recordings, percent correct is 70.7% (all trials pooled) to 75.5% (control trials, mean over sessions), within 77.6 +/- 7.8%, but lick-early trials are 14.7 to 18.2% against 10.3 +/- 1.0%, and no-response trials 0.73 to 0.98% against 1.1 +/- 0.11%. No reading puts all three within tolerance, and two of the three values are outside it under every reading of the full set of recordings. The whole-cell recordings alone come closest (77.4 to 83.5% correct, 7.9 to 9.7% lick early, 0.96 to 1.55% no response), with at most two values within tolerance. The dandiset holds recording sessions only, not the behaviour sessions the paper's averages may include. (Partially reproduced before the first verification; changed on the verifier's reading that no reading puts all three values within tolerance.)

fig1c-alm-photoinhibition-bias¶

Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch biased responses to the ipsilateral side, lowering performance on contra trials and raising it on ipsi trials.

The dandiset has no behaviour-only sessions; the test uses the behavioural trials of the 66 recording sessions in PV-Cre x Ai32 mice with left-ALM photoinhibition in the delay epoch (ALM, thalamic and SNr recordings, 13 mice). Main reading: photoinhibition trials at 1.5 mW (the Methods' power); variant: all delay-epoch powers (1.5 and 0.75/0.79 mW), outside the condition by convention P (answer of 2026-10-20). Per session, fraction correct with lick-early and no-response trials excluded; two-sided paired t-test over sessions.

In [11]:
def fig1c(stims):
    rows = []
    for s in sessions:
        m = s["meta"]
        if m["genotype"] != "Ai32 x PV-Cre" or m["ogen_site"] != "ALM":
            continue
        t = s["trials"]
        k = t.response.isin(loop.KEEP).values
        r = {"subject": m["subject"], "region": m["region"]}
        for side, con in (("contra", True), ("ipsi", False)):
            for cond, msk in (("ctrl", (t.stim == "none").values), ("pi", t.stim.isin(stims).values)):
                sel = k & msk & (t.contra.values == con)
                r[f"{side}_{cond}"] = (t.response.values[sel] == "correct").mean() if sel.any() else np.nan
                r[f"n_{side}_{cond}"] = int(sel.sum())
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


for name, stims in (("1.5 mW", ["ALM:delay:1.5"]), ("all delay powers", ["ALM:delay:1.5", "ALM:delay:0.79", "ALM:delay:0.75"])):
    d = fig1c(stims)
    full = d.dropna(subset=["contra_ctrl", "contra_pi", "ipsi_ctrl", "ipsi_pi"])
    print(f"--- {name}: {len(full)} of {len(d)} sessions with all four cells, {full.subject.nunique()} mice;"
          f" photoinhibition trials per session median {int((full.n_contra_pi + full.n_ipsi_pi).median())}")
    for side in ("contra", "ipsi"):
        tt = stats.ttest_rel(full[f"{side}_pi"], full[f"{side}_ctrl"])
        print(f"{side}: control {full[side + '_ctrl'].mean():.3f}, photoinhibition {full[side + '_pi'].mean():.3f}, "
              f"change {(full[side + '_pi'] - full[side + '_ctrl']).mean():+.3f} (sessions with an increase "
              f"{int((full[side + '_pi'] > full[side + '_ctrl']).sum())}/{len(full)}), paired t = {tt.statistic:.2f}, p = {tt.pvalue:.2g}")
    if name == "1.5 mW":
        print("Per mouse (means over sessions):")
        print(full.groupby("subject")[["contra_ctrl", "contra_pi", "ipsi_ctrl", "ipsi_pi"]].mean().round(3).assign(
            sessions=full.groupby("subject").size()).to_string())
        print("By recorded region:")
        print(full.groupby("region")[["contra_ctrl", "contra_pi", "ipsi_ctrl", "ipsi_pi"]].mean().round(3).to_string())

Result: reproduced. In 66 recording sessions of 11 PV-Cre x Ai32 mice, ALM photoinhibition at 1.5 mW lowers contra performance from 0.774 to 0.368 (paired t = -16.67, p = 3.6e-25; no session increases) and raises ipsi performance from 0.673 to 0.744 (t = 3.99, p = 0.00017; 46 of 66 sessions increase). Both hold at p < 0.001, and with all powers pooled (p = 4.7e-25 and 0.00054). These are the behavioural trials of recording sessions, not the paper's 84 behaviour sessions.

alm-unit-classes¶

Of 1214 ALM units, 1006 were putative pyramidal neurons (spike width > 0.6 ms), 166 putative fast-spiking (< 0.4 ms) and 42 unclassified; the spike-width distribution was bimodal.

Result: not reproduced. The dandiset holds 966 ALM units (paper 1214 +/- 121). The file labels give 810 wide and 121 narrow units (35 undetermined), fractions 0.839 and 0.125 against the paper's 0.829 and 0.137. Computed widths give 577 units above 0.6 ms and 127 below 0.4 ms, because the deposited waveforms are too short (514 of the 577 have their peak at the last sample). No count is within tolerance under either reading; P1 is the Methods' rule, and it fails because of the waveforms, not the units. The width histogram has two modes, at 0.28 ms (62 units) and 0.68 to 0.72 ms (267 and 249), with a trough at 0.36 ms (4 units).

The criterion has no partial clause, and no reading meets it in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

fig2e-alm-selectivity¶

Most ALM putative pyramidal neurons (70%, 704/1006) distinguished trial types; 145 had preparatory activity only, 272 peri-movement selectivity only and 287 both.

Every reading of the criterion (trials control or all; R1, R2; Student, Welch; c1, c2), for both unit readings P1 and P2.

In [13]:
def sel_counts(idx, key):
    d = SEL[key].loc[idx]
    return {"n": len(d), "selective": int(d.selective.sum()), "prep_only": int((d.kind == "prep_only").sum()),
            "peri_only": int((d.kind == "peri_only").sum()), "both": int((d.kind == "both").sum()),
            "contra_pref": int((d.selective & d.contra_pref).sum())}


rows = []
for p, d in PYR.items():
    for k in SEL:
        rows.append({"units": p, "reading": k, **sel_counts(d.index, k)})
f2e = pd.DataFrame(rows)
f2e["frac_selective"] = (f2e.selective / f2e.n).round(3)
f2e["within_tol"] = ((f2e.selective - 704).abs() <= 70) & ((f2e.prep_only - 145).abs() <= 15) & \
    ((f2e.peri_only - 272).abs() <= 27) & ((f2e.both - 287).abs() <= 29)
for col, ref in (("selective", 704), ("prep_only", 145), ("peri_only", 272), ("both", 287)):
    f2e[col + "_scaled"] = (f2e[col] * 1006 / f2e.n).round(0)
print(f2e.to_string(index=False))
print("Paper: 704/1006 selective (0.70), 145 prep only, 272 peri only, 287 both")
print("Readings with all four counts within tolerance:", int(f2e.within_tol.sum()), "of", len(f2e))
k0 = "control/R1/Student/c1"
print(f"\nBy mouse ({k0}, P2):")
d = SEL[k0].loc[PYR["P2"].index].join(PYR["P2"][["subject", "genotype"]])
print(d.groupby(["genotype", "subject"]).agg(n=("selective", "size"), selective=("selective", "mean")).round(3).to_string())

fig2e-alm-contra-ipsi-balance¶

Approximately equal numbers of selective ALM neurons preferred contra and ipsi movements.

Readings: (a) two-sided binomial test of the contra count against one half does not reject at p < 0.05; (b) the contra fraction lies within 0.45 to 0.55. Under each reading of fig2e-alm-selectivity.

In [14]:
bal = f2e[["units", "reading", "selective", "contra_pref"]].copy()
bal["contra_frac"] = (bal.contra_pref / bal.selective).round(3)
bal["binom_p"] = [stats.binomtest(int(c), int(n), 0.5).pvalue for c, n in zip(bal.contra_pref, bal.selective)]
bal["a_binomial_holds"] = bal.binom_p >= 0.05
bal["b_fraction_holds"] = bal.contra_frac.between(0.45, 0.55)
print(bal.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("Readings where (a) holds:", int(bal.a_binomial_holds.sum()), "| (b) holds:", int(bal.b_fraction_holds.sum()), "| of", len(bal))
print("Contra fraction range:", bal.contra_frac.min(), "to", bal.contra_frac.max())

Of 790 thalamic units, 672 were putative thalamic neurons (spike width > 0.5 ms) and 313 lay within 0.4 mm of the VM/VAL centre; 295 VM/VAL units were analysed.

fig2f-vmval-selectivity¶

A majority of VM/VAL neurons (69%, 204/295) distinguished trial types, a fraction indistinguishable from ALM; 43 had preparatory activity only, 82 peri-movement selectivity only and 79 both, a distribution similar to ALM.

VM/VAL units of thalamus-unit-classes (L2), under every selectivity reading and P1, P2, and P3 (all VM/VAL units, compared with ALM P1 and P2). Chi-squared tests against ALM pyramidal units under the same readings: 2 x 2 (selective or not), and for the types (i) 2 x 4 with non-selective as a class, (ii) 2 x 3 among selective neurons.

In [16]:
rows = []
for p, pa in (("P1", "P1"), ("P2", "P2"), ("P3", "P1"), ("P3", "P2")):
    for k in SEL:
        v, a = sel_counts(VM26[p].index, k), sel_counts(PYR[pa].index, k)
        chi_sel = stats.chi2_contingency([[v["selective"], v["n"] - v["selective"]], [a["selective"], a["n"] - a["selective"]]])[1]
        t4 = [[v["prep_only"], v["peri_only"], v["both"], v["n"] - v["selective"]], [a["prep_only"], a["peri_only"], a["both"], a["n"] - a["selective"]]]
        chi4 = stats.chi2_contingency(t4)[1]
        chi3 = stats.chi2_contingency([r[:3] for r in t4])[1]
        rows.append({"units": p, "alm_units": pa, "reading": k, **{x: v[x] for x in ("n", "selective", "prep_only", "peri_only", "both")},
                     "frac": round(v["selective"] / v["n"], 3), "alm_frac": round(a["selective"] / a["n"], 3),
                     "p_chi_selective": chi_sel, "p_chi_2x4": chi4, "p_chi_2x3": chi3})
f2f = pd.DataFrame(rows)
f2f["counts_within_tol"] = ((f2f.selective - 204).abs() <= 20) & ((f2f.prep_only - 43).abs() <= 4.3) & \
    ((f2f.peri_only - 82).abs() <= 8.2) & ((f2f.both - 79).abs() <= 7.9)
f2f["chi_ok_i"] = (f2f.p_chi_selective >= 0.05) & (f2f.p_chi_2x4 >= 0.05)
f2f["chi_ok_ii"] = (f2f.p_chi_selective >= 0.05) & (f2f.p_chi_2x3 >= 0.05)
print(f2f.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("Paper: 204/295 (0.69), 43, 82, 79; chi-squared p = 0.79 (fraction), p > 0.5 (types)")
print("Readings with counts within tolerance:", int(f2f.counts_within_tol.sum()), "| with both chi-squared tests p >= 0.05 (i):",
      int(f2f.chi_ok_i.sum()), "(ii):", int(f2f.chi_ok_ii.sum()), "| all of counts and (i) or (ii):",
      int((f2f.counts_within_tol & (f2f.chi_ok_i | f2f.chi_ok_ii)).sum()), "of", len(f2f))
print("\nBy VM/VAL unit reading (ALM reading in brackets): selective fraction range, readings with counts within tolerance,"
      " readings with the 2 x 2 test p >= 0.05, with (i) and with (ii) holding")
print(f2f.groupby(["units", "alm_units"]).agg(frac_min=("frac", "min"), frac_max=("frac", "max"), n=("n", "first"),
                                             counts_ok=("counts_within_tol", "sum"), chi_sel_ok=("p_chi_selective", lambda x: int((x >= 0.05).sum())),
                                             ok_i=("chi_ok_i", "sum"), ok_ii=("chi_ok_ii", "sum"), readings=("frac", "size")).to_string())
print("Scaled to 295 units: selective", (f2f.selective * 295 / f2f.n).round(0).min(), "to", (f2f.selective * 295 / f2f.n).round(0).max())

Result: not reproduced. With P2, 149 of 222 VM/VAL units (67%) are selective under the first reading (paper 204/295, 69%), and the fraction does not differ from ALM's 70.5% (chi-squared p = 0.37). The selectivity types differ from ALM in all 16 P2 readings (both type tests p < 0.05; first reading 38 preparatory only, 75 peri-movement only, 36 both, p = 0.011 and 0.0053), where the paper finds p > 0.5. With P3 (all 259 VM/VAL units), 174 are selective under the first reading (67%; 156 to 177 over the readings, below 204 +/- 20), the fraction does not differ from ALM in any reading, and the types differ from ALM in all 32 readings (first reading 40, 89, 45; p = 0.024 and 0.0098 against ALM P1). The counts are below tolerance in every reading; with P1 only 20 units qualify, and their types do not differ from ALM. The selective fraction holds; the type distribution holds only on the 20 P1 units.

The criterion has no partial clause, and no reading meets it in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

fig3-alm-collapse¶

Strong photoinhibition of thalALM (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP) decreased ALM activity to 6% of control, inhibiting 309 of 314 neurons (155 significantly) and significantly activating none.

ALM putative pyramidal units of the VGAT-ChR2-EYFP sessions (thalamus photostimulus, 10 mW, delay epoch), at least 5 photostimulus trials; 20 to 120 ms after onset; readings T1 (correct and incorrect) and T2 (correct only), Q1 to Q3, Student and Welch, P1 and P2. Variant, not part of the criterion: the ALM sessions of PV-Cre x Ai32 mice with thalamic photostimulation at 10 mW, which the answer of 2026-10-20 places outside Fig. 3.

In [17]:
T_READ = {"T1": ("correct", "incorrect"), "T2": ("correct",)}


def effect_table(sel_units, stims, window="pw", min_trials=5, extra=None):
    rows, keep = [], {}
    for p, d in sel_units.items():
        for tname, oc in T_READ.items():
            for ev in (True, False):
                df = loop.photo_effect(sessions, d, stims, oc, window, min_trials, ev)
                keep[(p, tname, ev)] = df
                rows.append({"units": p, "trials": tname, "test": "Student" if ev else "Welch", **loop.effect_counts(df),
                             **{k: round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in loop.ratio_readings(df).items()},
                             "mice": d.loc[df.index].subject.nunique()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), keep


vg_alm = {p: d[d.genotype == "VGAT-ChR2-EYFP"] for p, d in PYR.items()}
f3, F3 = effect_table(vg_alm, "Thalamus:delay:10")
for q in ("Q1", "Q2", "Q3"):
    f3[f"within_tol_{q}"] = ((f3[q] - 6).abs() <= 0.6) & ((f3.n - 314).abs() <= 31) & ((f3.inhibited - 309).abs() <= 31) & \
        ((f3.activated - 3).abs() <= 0.3) & ((f3.sig_inhibited - 155).abs() <= 16) & (f3.sig_activated == 0)
print(f3.to_string(index=False))
print("Paper: 6% of control; 314 neurons, 309 inhibited, 3 activated, 155 significantly inhibited, 0 significantly activated")
print("Readings within tolerance on all values:", int(f3[[c for c in f3 if c.startswith("within_tol")]].any(axis=1).sum()), "of", len(f3))
print("Partial condition (activity falls, inhibited > activated, none significantly activated) in every reading:",
      bool(((f3.Q1 < 100) & (f3.inhibited > f3.activated) & (f3.sig_activated == 0)).all()))
d = F3[("P2", "T1", True)].join(units[["subject"]])
print("\nBy mouse (P2, T1, Student):")
print(d.groupby("subject").agg(n=("delta", "size"), inhibited=("delta", lambda x: int((x < 0).sum())),
                               rate_ctrl=("rate_ctrl", "mean"), rate_pi=("rate_pi", "mean")).round(2).to_string())
pv_alm = {p: d[(d.genotype == "Ai32 x PV-Cre") & (d.ogen_site == "Thalamus")] for p, d in PYR.items()}
v3, _ = effect_table(pv_alm, "Thalamus:delay:10")
print("\nVariant, PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions with thalamic photostimulation at 10 mW:")
print(v3.to_string(index=False))
both = {p: pd.concat([vg_alm[p], pv_alm[p]]) for p in PYR}
v3b, _ = effect_table(both, "Thalamus:delay:10")
print("Variant, VGAT and PV-Cre x Ai32 together at 10 mW:")
print(v3b.to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. In 261 VGAT ALM putative pyramidal units (P2; 234 with P1) from 3 mice, thalamus photoinhibition lowers activity to 2.1 to 2.5% (Q1) or 5.1 to 5.2% (Q2) of control, against 6 +/- 0.6%. With P2 and correct and incorrect trials, 256 of 261 units are inhibited, 2 activated, 127 (Student) or 208 (Welch) significantly inhibited and none significantly activated. The number of units (230 to 261) is below 314 +/- 31, and no reading puts all values within tolerance. The criterion's partial condition (activity falls, inhibited outnumber activated, none significantly activated) holds in every reading. In the variant with the PV-Cre x Ai32 sessions at 10 mW, activity falls to 21.7% (P2, T1) and 7 units are significantly activated.

fig3d-all-layers¶

Thalamus photoinhibition reduced ALM activity across all cortical layers.

Units of fig3-alm-collapse; depth is -unit_y (mm). Bins (a) 100 um, (b) 200 um; modulated (m1) by the sign of the change, (m2) significant by convention P. Per bin, inhibited against activated neurons, and the population rate ratio.

rows = []
for p in ("P1", "P2"):
    for tname in T_READ:
        for mod, ev in (("m1", True), ("m2 Student", True), ("m2 Welch", False)):
            df = F3[(p, tname, ev)].join(units[["dv"]])
            depth = -df.dv * 1000
            for bw in (100, 200):
                b = (depth // bw * bw).astype(int)
                for lo, g in df.groupby(b):
                    sel = g.sig if mod != "m1" else np.ones(len(g), bool)
                    inh, act = int(((g.delta < 0) & sel).sum()), int(((g.delta > 0) & sel).sum())

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Counting by the sign of the change (m1), inhibited neurons outnumber activated ones in every depth bin under every reading (12 of 12 bins of 100 um, 7 of 7 of 200 um), and the population rate under photoinhibition is at most 0.205 of control in any bin. Counting significant changes (m2), 1 to 3 bins fail with Student's test and 1 with Welch's, each holding 1 to 4 neurons with no significant change in either direction (0 against 0). The criterion asks every reading to agree, so the claim is blocked as it directs. The reduction itself is seen at every depth sampled (101 to 1212 um of -unit_y). The files describe unit_y only as "y-coordinate of this unit (mm)", so whether it is depth below the pia is not stated.

fig3b-selectivity-types-equally-inhibited¶

ALM neurons with preparatory activity, peri-movement selectivity or both were equally inhibited by thalamus photoinhibition.

A claim of absence, on the paper's test: two-sided t-tests between each pair of the three groups, measures (a) rate ratio and (b) rate difference, for the neurons of fig3-alm-collapse. Shown under every selectivity reading, both trial readings and P1, P2 (Student's t-test for the group comparison; Welch shown as a count).

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Under the first selectivity reading both measures find a difference between groups: the rate difference (p < 0.0001 between peri-movement-only and both) and the rate ratio (p = 0.016 with P1, 0.010 with P2, T1). Over all readings the difference measure finds one in all 64 combinations and the ratio measure in 13, so the two measures disagree in most readings, which the criterion calls methods underspecified. No reading supports equal inhibition under the difference measure.

Result: not reproduced. Putative thalamic units of the VGAT sessions fall to 1.1% (T1) or 0.9% (T2) of control (Q1; Q2 0.9 to 1.4%), on 113 units (P2) or 93 (P1) against 148 +/- 15; none is activated, and 101 of 113 are significantly inhibited (P2, T1, Student). With all units (134 under T1) the count is within tolerance but narrow units raise Q1 to 18%. The silencing is nearly complete, as the paper says, but the 2% and the unit count are not both within tolerance under any reading. No VGAT thalamic unit lies within 0.4 mm of the L2 centre, so reading (b) has no units.

The criterion has no partial clause, and no reading meets it in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

vgat-thalamus-reduction¶

In VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, thalamus photoinhibition reduced activity 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre tip to 15.9% of control.

Putative thalamic units of the VGAT thalamic sessions, at 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre. The files give one photostimulus site for every session (AP -1.5, ML 0.9, DV -4.1 mm), a nominal coordinate; distance from it is computed in 3 dimensions and in the coronal plane (ML, DV). Windows W1 (whole delay epoch) and W2 (20 to 120 ms), T1, T2, Q1 to Q3.

In [21]:
fib = np.array([0.9, -4.1, -1.5])
rows = []
for p, d in {**vg_th, **vg_th_all}.items():
    d3 = np.sqrt((d.ml.abs() - fib[0]) ** 2 + (d.dv - fib[1]) ** 2 + (d.ap - fib[2]) ** 2)
    d2 = np.hypot(d.ml.abs() - fib[0], d.dv - fib[1])
    for dname, dist in (("3D", d3), ("coronal", d2)):
        sub = d[(dist >= 0.5) & (dist <= 1.1)]
        groups = np.select([dist < 0.7, dist < 0.9], ["0.6", "0.8"], "1.0")
        for wname, win, mx in (("W1", "delay", None), ("W2", "pw", None), ("variant: W1, 1.3 s delays only", "delay", 1.35)):
            for tname, oc in T_READ.items():
                df = loop.photo_effect(sessions, sub, "Thalamus:delay:2.23", oc, win, 5, True, max_delay=mx)
                r = loop.ratio_readings(df)

tcb = loop.TC_SPAN[0] + loop.BIN_S * np.arange(int(round((loop.TC_SPAN[1] - loop.TC_SPAN[0]) / loop.BIN_S)))
binrows = []
for dname, lo, hi in (("1.3 s delay", 0, 1.35), ("delay > 1.35 s", 1.35, 99)):
    rc, rp = [], []
    for r in sub.itertuples():
        s = sessions[r.session]
        t = s["trials"]
        m = t.response.isin(loop.KEEP).values & s["valid"][r.unit] & t.tc_ok.values & (t.delay_s.values > lo) & (t.delay_s.values <= hi)
        c_, p_ = m & (t.stim == "none").values, m & (t.stim == "Thalamus:delay:2.23").values
        if p_.sum() < 1 or c_.sum() < 1:
            continue
        rc.append(s["tc"][r.unit][c_].mean(0) / loop.BIN_S)
        rp.append(s["tc"][r.unit][p_].mean(0) / loop.BIN_S)
    if not rc:
        binrows.append({"trials": dname, "units": 0})
        continue
    rc, rp = np.array(rc), np.array(rp)
    q1 = 100 * rp.mean(0) / rc.mean(0)
    binrows.append({"trials": dname, "units": len(rc), **{f"{x:.1f}": round(float(q1[np.argmin(np.abs(tcb - x))]), 1) for x in np.arange(1.0, 4.05, 0.2)}})

Result: reproduced. Over the whole photostimulus (W1), putative thalamic units 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre site fall to 17.0 to 20.3% (Q1) or 16.5 to 19.3% (Q3) of control, within 15.9 +/- 9.3%; Q2 is 37.5 to 51.2%. In the 20 to 120 ms window (W2) they fall to 1.2 to 1.5% (Q1). Every trial of the VGAT thalamic sessions has a 1.3 s delay, so W1 ends with the delay epoch and holds no time after the photostimulus; restricting W1 to 1.3 s delays changes nothing. In 100 ms bins the ratio is 21.6% in the first bin after 1.4 s, falls to 9 to 11% by the end of the delay and returns to 100% in the first bin of the response epoch: activity, silenced at first (W2), partly recovers during the photostimulus. 63 to 79 units qualify against the paper's 114, the site is one nominal coordinate for all sessions, so the distances are approximate, and the files give the power as 2.23 mW where the paper gives 10 mW.

fig3-onset-latencies¶

Photoinhibition reduced thalALM activity 2.5 ms after photostimulus onset, and ALM spike rates were reduced 8.2 ms after onset, a latency difference consistent with direct thalamocortical drive.

Convention O on population PSTHs (1 ms bins), readings O1 and O2, T1 and T2; the thalamic population of fig3f-thalamus-silenced (putative thalamic units, reading a) and the ALM population of fig3-alm-collapse, both with at least 5 photostimulus trials; SEM from 1000 resamplings of units. P1 and P2.

rng = np.random.default_rng(301)


def onset_rows(label, sel, stims, direction=-1, flip=None):
    rows = []
    if len(sel) == 0:
        return [{"population": label, "n": 0}]
    for tname, oc in T_READ.items():
        c, p = loop.population_psth(sessions, sel, stims, oc)
        if flip is not None:
            p = np.where(flip[:, None], 2 * c - p, p)
        for rd in ("O1", "O2"):
            est, sem, nan = loop.bootstrap_onset(c, p, rd, rng, 1000, direction)
            rows.append({"population": label, "n": len(sel), "trials": tname, "reading": rd, "onset_ms": est, "sem_ms": round(sem, 2),
                         "boot_no_onset": nan})
    return rows

    rows += onset_rows(f"ALM VGAT {p}", alm_units, "Thalamus:delay:10")

Result: reproduced. Under reading O2 with correct and incorrect trials (T1), the thalamic onset is 2.0 ms (SEM 1.08 with P1, 0.96 with P2) and the ALM onset 9.0 ms (P1, SEM 3.68) or 7.0 ms (P2, SEM 3.16), within 2.5 +/- 0.8 and 8.2 +/- 1.5 ms, with ALM later. The other readings fail: under O1 the ALM onset is 0 ms in three of four cases (the first 1 ms bin already lies 3 SD below control), and under T2 with O2 it is 6 ms. The pass rests on one reading of four and the rule is fragile: on photostimulus PSTHs simulated from each unit's control PSTH with no effect, it still reports an onset in every run, below 10 ms in 30 to 48% of them; with a simulated step at 8 ms it reports an onset before 8 ms in 18 to 43% of runs and within 6.5 to 9.5 ms in 60 to 84%. The ALM onset of 0 ms under O1 is such a false onset. The bootstrap SEMs of the ALM onset under T1 and O2 (3.2 and 3.7 ms) are twice the paper's 1.5 ms.

fig6c-vmval-reduced¶

ALM photoinhibition decreased the activity of VM/VAL neurons to 25% of control, inhibiting 190 of 201 neurons (139 significantly) and significantly activating none.

P3 (all VM/VAL units regardless of width) as a further unit reading. Variant: all ALM photoinhibition powers (1.5 and 0.79 mW).

Result: not reproduced. In 172 VM/VAL putative units (P2, T1; 15 with P1) from 7 mice, ALM photoinhibition at 1.5 mW lowers activity to 47.5% (Q1), 46.5% (Q2) or 36.4% (Q3) of control, against 25%: 151 are inhibited, 21 activated, 99 (Student) or 105 (Welch) significantly inhibited and 2 significantly activated. With P3 (all VM/VAL units, T1) 201 units qualify, the paper's n, and 173 are inhibited (190 +/- 19), but activity falls only to 55.9% (Q1) or 40.0% (Q3), 28 are activated and 4 or 5 significantly activated. No reading puts every value within tolerance, and the partial condition fails because under P2 and P3 1 to 5 units are significantly activated (it holds in the 4 P1 readings only). The reduction is present, about half as deep as the paper's.

fig6b-selectivity-types-equally-inhibited¶

VM/VAL neurons selective during the sample, delay or response epochs were equally inhibited by ALM photoinhibition.

Neurons of fig6c-vmval-reduced. Groups (a) preparatory only, peri-movement only, both; (b) selective in the sample, the delay, the response epoch (overlapping). Measures ratio and difference; two-sided t-tests between each pair; every selectivity reading, T1 and T2, P1, P2 and P3.

rows = []
for p in ("P1", "P2", "P3"):
    for tname in T_READ:
        eff = F6[(p, tname, True)]
        for k in SEL:
            st = SEL[k].loc[eff.index]
            grp_a = {n: st.kind == n for n in ("prep_only", "peri_only", "both")}
            grp_b = {"sample": st.p_sample < 0.05, "delay": st.p_delay < 0.05, "response": st.p_resp < 0.05}
            for gname, grp in (("a", grp_a), ("b", grp_b)):
                for meas in ("ratio", "delta"):
                    g = {n: eff[meas][m].dropna() for n, m in grp.items()}
                    names = list(g)
                    ps = [stats.ttest_ind(g[x], g[y]).pvalue if min(len(g[x]), len(g[y])) > 1 else np.nan
                          for i, x in enumerate(names) for y in names[i + 1:]]
                    rows.append({"units": p, "trials": tname, "sel_reading": k, "groups": gname, "measure": meas,
                                 "n": tuple(len(v) for v in g.values()), "means": tuple(round(v.mean(), 2) for v in g.values()),
                                 "min_p": np.nanmin(ps) if np.isfinite(ps).any() else np.nan})

fig6c-unmodulated-less-selective¶

The few VM/VAL neurons not changed by ALM photoinhibition were significantly less selective in the delay epoch, while neurons strongly reduced by it carried trial-type information; the change of rate and delay selectivity were negatively related (regression slope -0.73, r -0.33).

Neurons of fig6c-vmval-reduced split by the significance of their change. Delay selectivity on correct control trials, (a) |contra - ipsi| rate, (b) preferred minus non-preferred rate (preference by total count, convention S). Two-sided t-test; regression (i) selectivity on change, (ii) change on selectivity. P1, P2 and P3.

rows = []
for p in ("P1", "P2", "P3"):
    for tname in T_READ:
        for ev in (True, False):
            eff = F6[(p, tname, ev)]
            rc, ri = [], []
            for idx in eff.index:
                r = units.loc[idx]
                s = sessions[r.session]
                t = s["trials"]
                m = (t.response == "correct").values & (t.stim == "none").values
                c = s["counts"]["delay"][r.unit] / t.delay_s.values
                rc.append(np.nanmean(c[m & t.contra.values]))
                ri.append(np.nanmean(c[m & ~t.contra.values]))
            rc, ri = np.array(rc), np.array(ri)
            pref = SEL["control/R1/Student/c1"].loc[eff.index, "contra_pref"].values
            sel = {"a": np.abs(rc - ri), "b": np.where(pref, rc - ri, ri - rc)}
            for sname, sv in sel.items():
                tt = stats.ttest_ind(sv[eff.sig.values], sv[~eff.sig.values], equal_var=ev)
                for ax in ("i", "ii"):
                    x, y = (eff.delta.values, sv) if ax == "i" else (sv, eff.delta.values)
                    lr = stats.linregress(x, y)
                    rows.append({"units": p, "trials": tname, "test": "Student" if ev else "Welch", "selectivity": sname, "axes": ax,
                                 "n_sig": int(eff.sig.sum()), "n_not": int((~eff.sig).sum()),
                                 "sel_sig": round(sv[eff.sig.values].mean(), 2), "sel_not": round(sv[~eff.sig.values].mean(), 2),
                                 "t_p": tt.pvalue, "slope": round(lr.slope, 3), "r": round(lr.rvalue, 3)})
f6u = pd.DataFrame(rows)
f6u["group_ok"] = (f6u.sel_not < f6u.sel_sig) & (f6u.t_p < 0.05)
f6u["within_tol"] = f6u.group_ok & ((f6u.slope + 0.73).abs() <= 0.073) & ((f6u.r + 0.33).abs() <= 0.033)
f6u["partial"] = f6u.group_ok & (f6u.r < 0)
print(f6u.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("Paper: P = 0.002; slope -0.73, r -0.33")
print("Readings reproduced:", int(f6u.within_tol.sum()), "| partial:", int(f6u.partial.sum()), "| group difference holds:",
      int(f6u.group_ok.sum()), "of", len(f6u))
print(f6u.groupby("units").agg(readings=("r", "size"), group_ok=("group_ok", "sum"), partial=("partial", "sum"), within_tol=("within_tol", "sum"),
                               r_min=("r", "min"), r_max=("r", "max")).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. With P2 and correct and incorrect trials, the 71 neurons not significantly changed (Student) are less selective in the delay epoch than the 101 changed ones (|contra - ipsi| 1.13 against 1.77 spikes/s, p = 0.0030; the paper's P = 0.002), and the change of rate and delay selectivity are negatively correlated (r = -0.278 against -0.33 +/- 0.033; slope -0.074 with selectivity on change, -1.048 with change on selectivity, against -0.73). The group difference and a negative r hold in all 16 P2 readings, 12 of 16 P3 readings (r -0.142 to -0.201) and 4 of 16 P1 readings (P1 has 15 neurons); slope and r are out of tolerance in every reading.

fig6d-localized¶

The reduction of thalamic activity by ALM photoinhibition was mainly limited to VM/VAL; neurons within 1.0 mm of the VM/VAL centre were inhibited to 36% of control, and neurons farther away less.

Result: not reproduced. With P2 and the 20 to 120 ms window, ALM photoinhibition lowers thalamic activity to 48% (Q1) within 0.5 mm of the L2 centre, 62 to 65% at 0.5 to 1.0 mm and 81 to 85% at 1.0 mm or more: the reduction is concentrated near the centre. Within 1.0 mm it is to 52.6 to 53.4% (Q1) or 39.6 to 45.5% (Q3); only Q3 with correct trials (39.6%) is within 36 +/- 3.6%. With all units (u2, reading P3 of the answer) it is to 56.4 to 58.3% (Q1) or 44.2 to 48.2% (Q3). Near the centre the group counts (240 to 286) are within 250 +/- 25 except 286 (all units, correct and incorrect trials); farther away they (110 to 132, and 26 or 27) are below the paper's 160 and 46 in every reading, so no reading meets the whole criterion.

The criterion has no partial clause, and no reading meets it in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

vm1-photoinhibition-no-effect¶

Photoinhibiting vibrissal M1 did not reduce thalALM activity (Results), or reduced VM/VAL activity less than ALM photoinhibition in the same neurons (Extended Data Fig. 8g legend).

The dandiset names no vM1 site. In the six thalamic sessions of mouse anm00264943, photostimulation at galvo position (0.5, 0.5) mm is interleaved with ALM photoinhibition, which fits the interleaved design of Extended Data Fig. 8f, g; it is taken here as the vM1 condition, an assumption the files cannot confirm. The paper has 46 cells from 3 mice; here 1 mouse. (a) paired t-test over neurons of the rate under vM1 photoinhibition against control; (b) paired t-test of the reduction under vM1 against the reduction under ALM photoinhibition. ALM photoinhibition at 1.5 mW (convention P, answer of 2026-10-20); variants, not judged: ALM at 0.79 mW (the power of the (0.5, 0.5) trials) and both powers. Window 20 to 120 ms; T1 and T2; VM/VAL (L2) under P1, P2 and P3, and, as variants, all putative and all units of the mouse.

                rows.append({"units": sname, "trials": tname, "alm": aname, "n": len(j)})
                continue
            pa = stats.ttest_rel(v.loc[j, "rate_pi"], v.loc[j, "rate_ctrl"])
            pb = stats.ttest_rel(-v.loc[j, "delta"], -a.loc[j, "delta"])
            rows.append({"units": sname, "trials": tname, "alm": aname, "n": len(j),
                         "ctrl": round(v.loc[j, "rate_ctrl"].mean(), 2), "vM1": round(v.loc[j, "rate_pi"].mean(), 2), "ALM": round(a.loc[j, "rate_pi"].mean(), 2),
                         "vM1_Q1": round(100 * v.loc[j, "rate_pi"].mean() / v.loc[j, "rate_ctrl"].mean(), 1),
                         "ALM_Q1": round(100 * a.loc[j, "rate_pi"].mean() / a.loc[j, "rate_ctrl"].mean(), 1),
                         "vM1_Q3": round(100 * v.loc[j, "ratio"].median(), 1), "ALM_Q3": round(100 * a.loc[j, "ratio"].median(), 1),
                         "a_p": pa.pvalue, "a_vM1_reduces": bool(v.loc[j, "delta"].mean() < 0 and pa.pvalue < 0.05),
                         "b_p": pb.pvalue, "b_vM1_less": bool((-v.loc[j, "delta"]).mean() < (-a.loc[j, "delta"]).mean() and pb.pvalue < 0.05)})
vm1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(vm1.round(4).to_string(index=False))
m15 = vm1[vm1.alm == "ALM 1.5"]
print("ALM at 1.5 mW (convention P): rows where (a) no significant reduction under the (0.5, 0.5) site holds:",
      m15[~m15.a_vM1_reduces][["units", "trials"]].values.tolist(), "| where (b) holds:", m15[m15.b_vM1_less][["units", "trials"]].values.tolist())
print("Sessions of anm00264943 with (0.5, 0.5) trials:", sum(1 for s in sessions if (s["trials"].stim == "site0.5:delay:0.79").any()),
      "| trials:", sum(int((s["trials"].stim == "site0.5:delay:0.79").sum()) for s in sessions))

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient). The site at galvo (0.5, 0.5) mm is not named in the files, and the answer of 2026-10-20 says the paper does not say which condition is vM1. Taking it as vM1 and comparing with ALM at 1.5 mW, as the answer fixes: in 41 VM/VAL units (P2, T1) of one mouse it lowers activity to 89.6% of control (Q1; paired p = 0.058; T2 96.8%, p = 0.62), and ALM photoinhibition lowers the same units to 43.3%, a larger reduction (p < 0.0001). (a) and (b) hold together under P2 with T1 and T2 and under P3 with T2; under P3 with T1 (48 units) the (0.5, 0.5) site reduces activity significantly (90.4%, p = 0.040), so (a) fails there; under P1 only 3 units enter. In the variant with ALM at 0.79 mW the ALM reduction (91.6%, P2, T1) is no larger (p = 0.73). The paper's 46 cells come from 3 mice, these from 1.

snr-photoinhibition¶

ALM photoinhibition changed only a small fraction of SNr GABAergic neurons (48/181 significantly inhibited, 23/181 activated), more decreasing than increasing, and reduced SNr activity overall by 3.6 spikes per s (8.3%), which argues against SNr mediating the thalamic reduction.

SNr units of the dandiset (181; the paper's 46 wider units are not deposited, see snr-unit-properties) under P1 (< 0.45 ms, 171 units) and P2 (label 'Narrow width spiking', 146 units), and all 181 as a variant; ALM photoinhibition 1.5 mW, 20 to 120 ms; minimum photostimulus trials (a) none, (b) 5; T1, T2; Student, Welch. Bootstrap over neurons, 10000 rounds; p is the fraction of rounds with at least as many up- as down-modulated neurons.

rng = np.random.default_rng(601)
GABA["all 181"] = snr
rows, SNR = [], {}
for p, d in GABA.items():
    for mt in (0, 5):
        for tname, oc in T_READ.items():
            for ev in (True, False):
                df = loop.photo_effect(sessions, d, "ALM:delay:1.5", oc, "pw", mt, ev)
                SNR[(p, mt, tname, ev)] = df
                down = (df.sig & (df.delta < 0)).values
                up = (df.sig & (df.delta > 0)).values
                k = rng.integers(0, len(df), (10000, len(df)))
                pb = float(np.mean(up[k].sum(1) >= down[k].sum(1)))
                red = df.rate_ctrl.mean() - df.rate_pi.mean()
                rows.append({"units": p, "min_trials": mt, "trials": tname, "test": "Student" if ev else "Welch", "n": len(df),
                             "sig_inhibited": int(down.sum()), "sig_activated": int(up.sum()), "reduction": round(red, 2),

Result: not reproduced. The dandiset holds 181 SNr units, 171 under P1 and 146 under P2 (the 'Narrow width spiking' label); the paper's 46 wider units are not deposited (snr-unit-properties). Under P1 with correct and incorrect trials, 44 to 50 units are significantly inhibited and 21 activated (paper 48 and 23), and more decrease than increase (bootstrap p = 0.0003 to 0.0019); under P2, 35 to 40 and 18 (p = 0.0020 to 0.0105). The overall reduction is 2.25 to 2.44 spikes/s (5.8 to 6.3% of control) under P1 and 2.68 to 2.98 spikes/s (6.5 to 7.2%) under P2, against 3.6 spikes/s (8.3%), out of tolerance in every reading. Under P1 the counts and the test agree with the paper; the reduction is weaker.

The criterion has no partial clause, and no reading meets it in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

snr-unit-properties¶

Putative GABAergic SNr neurons had high spike rates (40.9 spikes per s) compared with the other SNr units (23.4), and most of them (152/181) were selective for trial type, like ALM and VM/VAL.

Mean rate per unit, (a) over the session (spikes over the time from the first trial start to the last trial end), (b) within trials (spikes in trials over the summed trial durations); then the mean over units. Selectivity by convention S under every reading.

Result: blocked (data missing). Spikes are stored for only about 5 s of each 9 s trial, so neither reading of the mean rate can be computed as defined; as computed, both give 20.7 (P1) or 22.0 (P2) spikes/s for the putative GABAergic units against 40.9, biased low because they divide by time with no stored spikes. Over the stored part of each trial (a variant, not deciding) the same units fire 36.0 (P1) or 38.1 (P2) spikes/s, and the other units 13.1 (10 units, P1) or 20.3 (35 units, P2) against 23.4. Only 10 (P1) or 35 (P2) other SNr units are deposited, against 46, and under P2 most of them are labelled 'Cannot be determined'. The selectivity count can be tested: 139 of 171 units (P1) are selective under the first reading, within 152 +/- 15 (137 to 143 in the eight c1 readings); under P2, 114 to 122 of 146, below it.

fig6e-onset-latencies¶

After ALM photoinhibition onset, ALM pyramidal neurons were silenced after 8.1 ms and VM/VAL activity reduced after 10.9 ms; SNr neurons changed later, after 15.2 ms.

Convention O (O1, O2), T1 and T2, bootstrap SEM (1000). Populations: ALM putative pyramidal units of the PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions with ALM photoinhibition at 1.5 mW (at least 5 trials; the paper has 256), VM/VAL units of fig6c-vmval-reduced (P1, P2, and P3 with the ALM P1 or P2 population), and the significantly modulated SNr units of snr-photoinhibition (P2, 5 trials, T1, Student): (a) inhibited only, (b) inhibited and activated with the sign of the activated flipped. Readings (d1) onsets from photostimulus onset; (d2) SNr and VM/VAL onsets minus the ALM onset.

No reading puts all three within tolerance with SNr latest.

selectivity-time-course¶

In ALM and in VM/VAL, population selectivity emerged in the sample epoch and increased throughout the delay epoch; it peaked at the beginning of the response epoch in ALM and during the response epoch in VM/VAL.

Extended Data Fig. 4c: per neuron, the preferred trial type from spike counts (sample, delay and response epochs, R1) in a random half of the correct trials, selectivity as preferred minus non-preferred rate in the other half, 200 ms windows stepped by 100 ms, SEM by bootstrapping over neurons (1000). Neurons (a) all, (b) selective (reading control/R1/Student/c1, the first of each list). Trials: readings (t1) correct control trials and (t2) all correct trials (answer of 2026-10-20). VM/VAL units under P1, P2 and P3 (all VM/VAL units). Only trials with a 1.3 s delay enter, so that the epochs align. "Emerged": mean above twice its SEM in a window inside the sample epoch; "increased": last 200 ms of the delay above the first; the maximum is located.

rng = np.random.default_rng(701)
tc_t = loop.TC_SPAN[0] + loop.BIN_S * np.arange(int(round((loop.TC_SPAN[1] - loop.TC_SPAN[0]) / loop.BIN_S)))
win_t = tc_t[:-1] + 0.1        # centre of each 200 ms window (two 100 ms bins)


def time_course(sel, ctrl_only):
    out = []
    for r in sel.itertuples():
        s = sessions[r.session]
        t = s["trials"]
        m = (t.response == "correct").values & (np.abs(t.delay_s.values - 1.3) < 0.05) & s["valid"][r.unit] & t.tc_ok.values
        if ctrl_only:
            m = m & (t.stim == "none").values
        ci, ii = np.flatnonzero(m & t.contra.values), np.flatnonzero(m & ~t.contra.values)
        if len(ci) < 4 or len(ii) < 4:
            continue
        ci, ii = rng.permutation(ci), rng.permutation(ii)
        ca, cb, ia, ib = ci[: len(ci) // 2], ci[len(ci) // 2:], ii[: len(ii) // 2], ii[len(ii) // 2:]
        tot = s["counts"]["sample"][r.unit] + s["counts"]["delay"][r.unit] + s["counts"]["R1"][r.unit]
        pref_c = tot[ca].mean() >= tot[ia].mean()
        x = s["tc"][r.unit].astype(float)
        w2 = (x[:, :-1] + x[:, 1:]) / 0.2
        sel_ = w2[cb].mean(0) - w2[ib].mean(0)
        out.append(sel_ if pref_c else -sel_)
    return np.array(out)


rows = []
curves = {}
for area, base in (("ALM P1", PYR["P1"]), ("ALM P2", PYR["P2"]), ("VM/VAL P1", VMVAL["P1"]), ("VM/VAL P2", VMVAL["P2"]),
                   ("VM/VAL P3", VM26["P3"])):
    for nsel in ("a", "b"):
        sel = base if nsel == "a" else base[SEL["control/R1/Student/c1"].loc[base.index, "selective"]]
        for ctrl_only in (True, False):
            tc = time_course(sel, ctrl_only)
            mean = tc.mean(0)
            boot = np.array([tc[rng.integers(0, len(tc), len(tc))].mean(0) for _ in range(1000)])
            sem = boot.std(0)
            in_sample = (win_t - 0.1 >= 0) & (win_t + 0.1 <= 1.3)
            emerged = bool((mean[in_sample] > 2 * sem[in_sample]).any())
            first_d = np.argmin(np.abs(win_t - 1.4))
            last_d = np.argmin(np.abs(win_t - 2.5))
            imax = int(np.argmax(mean))
            tmax = win_t[imax]
            epoch = "sample" if tmax < 1.3 else "delay" if tmax < 2.6 else "response"
            curves[(area, nsel, ctrl_only)] = (mean, sem)
            rows.append({"area": area, "neurons": nsel, "trials": "t1 correct control" if ctrl_only else "t2 all correct", "n": len(tc),
                         "first_emerging_window_s": round(float(win_t[in_sample][mean[in_sample] > 2 * sem[in_sample]][0]), 2) if emerged else np.nan,
                         "emerged_in_sample": emerged, "delay_first": round(mean[first_d], 2), "delay_last": round(mean[last_d], 2),
                         "increased": bool(mean[last_d] > mean[first_d]), "max_at_s": round(float(tmax), 2), "max_epoch": epoch,
                         "max_within_first_200ms_of_response": bool(2.6 <= tmax <= 2.8), "max_value": round(float(mean[imax]), 2)})
stc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(stc.to_string(index=False))
print("Time from pole onset: sample 0 to 1.3 s, delay 1.3 to 2.6 s, response from 2.6 s; window centres from",
      round(win_t[0], 2), "to", round(win_t[-1], 2), "s")
ok = stc.emerged_in_sample & stc.increased & (stc.max_epoch == "response")
print("Rows meeting all three:", stc[ok][["area", "neurons", "trials"]].values.tolist())

       for tr in ("t1 correct control", "t2 all correct")
       if ok[(stc.area == pa) & (stc.neurons == nsel) & (stc.trials == tr)].all() and ok[(stc.area == pv) & (stc.neurons == nsel) & (stc.trials == tr)].all()])

for key, col in ((("ALM P2", "a", True), "k"), (("VM/VAL P2", "a", True), "tab:blue")):

Result: reproduced. Under P3 for VM/VAL (all 258 VM/VAL units, all correct trials, t2) with ALM P2 (810 units, t2), both areas meet the criterion: selectivity emerges in the sample epoch (first window above twice its SEM centred at 0.1 s in ALM, 0.3 s in VM/VAL), is higher at the end of the delay than at its start (ALM 0.85 to 1.10, VM/VAL -0.05 to 0.38 spikes/s), and peaks in the response epoch (3.0 and 3.3 s). Six combinations of readings meet it in both areas, all with VM/VAL P3 (all neurons with t2, selective neurons with t1 and t2) and ALM P1 or P2. With P1 or P2, VM/VAL selectivity is lower at the end of the delay than at its start in every reading (P2, all neurons, t1: 0.83 against 0.17), and with P3, all neurons and t1 as well (0.57 against 0.53), so the delay increase in VM/VAL holds in 3 of 12 VM/VAL readings. The ALM peak lies 0.4 to 0.6 s after the go cue, not within its first 200 ms. Only trials whose spikes are stored to 4.1 s after pole onset enter.

wc-near-threshold¶

During the delay epoch the mean membrane potential of ALM neurons was close to spike threshold, 12.7 mV below it on average.

All 36 whole-cell recordings (each has more than 20 kept trials). Threshold: Vm at the kink of convention V, mean over the cell's spikes (all spikes in the recording). Basal Vm: (a) 0 to 0.5 s before trial onset (start_time), kept trials; (b) the delay epoch of kept control trials, spikes clipped. Per cell threshold minus basal, then the mean over cells with its SEM. Variants: the deposited kink (first sample of each clipped stretch plus 0.5 ms), and (a) without cell_21_1, whose trial start times are shifted by one row.

Whole-cell photoinhibition: wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization, wc-m1-small-effect, wc-contra-alm-small-effect, thalamus-stronger-than-cortex¶

wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization: Thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarized ALM neurons by 18.7 mV, preventing spiking, with an onset 7.9 ms after photostimulus onset.

wc-m1-small-effect: Photoinhibition of M1 during the delay epoch caused only a slight hyperpolarization (3.3 mV) and a small drop in spike rate (1.4 spikes per s) in ALM neurons.

wc-contra-alm-small-effect: Photoinhibition of contralateral ALM barely changed the membrane potential of ALM neurons (1.4 mV).

thalamus-stronger-than-cortex: thalALM drives ALM more strongly than M1 or contralateral ALM, the other reciprocally connected structures tested.

The claims file (answer of 2026-10-20) gives two readings of the photostimulus onset: E, 1.3 s after pole_in_time, and M, 0.1 s after pole_out_time. The files also hold the laser trace (data check), whose onset is reading L, shown here pending question 7. Each measure is computed under all three. Per cell: mean Vm (spikes clipped) 20 to 120 ms after the onset, photostimulus minus control kept trials, and the spike rate in the same window; then mean and SEM over cells. Onsets by convention V (V1 on the cell-mean trace, SEM from 1000 resamplings of cells; V2 the mean of per-cell onsets) are shown under every reading; the claims file says the 7.9 ms latency needs the laser time, which none of its readings gives, so the onset is not judged; it is shown under L pending question 7.

        dv, dsp, mean_tr, sp_c, sp_p = [], [], [], [], []
        onsets = []
        for c in cs:
            t = c["trials"]
            k = t.response.isin(loop.KEEP).values
            pi, ct = k & t.pi.values, k & ~t.pi.values
            dv.append(t[f"vm_pw_{reading}"][pi].mean() - t[f"vm_pw_{reading}"][ct].mean())
            dsp.append((t[f"spikes_pw_{reading}"][pi].mean() - t[f"spikes_pw_{reading}"][ct].mean()) / (loop.PW[1] - loop.PW[0]))

Result: wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization not reproduced; wc-m1-small-effect not reproduced; wc-contra-alm-small-effect reproduced; thalamus-stronger-than-cortex reproduced. Under onset E the window lies before the change (data check) and no value is within tolerance: thalamus photoinhibition changes Vm by +0.31 mV, M1 by -0.09 mV and +0.94 spikes/s, contralateral ALM by +0.86 mV, and thalamus is not more negative than the others (p = 0.41 to 0.58).

Under the laser onset (L), thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarizes ALM neurons by -13.68 +/- 1.14 mV, outside -18.7 +/- 1.1, and spiking stops (3.24 to 0.14 spikes/s); every one of the 16 cells hyperpolarizes (-4.7 to -21.7 mV). The onset is 9.60 +/- 1.98 ms by V2, within 7.9 +/- 1.7, and 0.40 ms by V1, which is not (five cells give 0.40 to 0.45 ms, at the laser onset itself). Under M, whose window starts 28 ms later in these cells, the change is -16.83 +/- 1.24 mV, also outside. The hyperpolarization and the loss of spiking are present at 73% (L) or 90% (M) of the paper's size; no reading puts both values within tolerance.

M1 photoinhibition changes Vm by -3.26 +/- 1.08 mV under L (-2.75 under M), within -3.3 +/- 1.0, and the spike rate by -0.01 +/- 1.16 spikes/s under L (+0.76 under M), outside -1.4 +/- 0.6: the slight hyperpolarization holds, the drop in spike rate is not seen. Contralateral ALM photoinhibition changes Vm by -1.38 +/- 0.58 mV under L and -1.60 +/- 0.64 under M, within -1.4 +/- 0.5. Thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarizes more than M1 or contralateral ALM photoinhibition under L (p = 1.3e-6 and 8.1e-8, Student; 6.7e-7 and 3.7e-9, Welch) and under M (p = 5e-8 and 8e-9, Student), so readings (a) and (b) both hold. The outcomes are the same under M and under L.

Neither wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization nor wc-m1-small-effect has a partial clause, and no reading meets either criterion in full (see Changes of outcome, before the Summary). The third verification round agreed.

For indirect-pathway-too-slow (blocked: no M1 neurons are deposited), the ALM onset after M1 photoinhibition under L is 8.7 +/- 4.6 ms (V1) or 27.3 +/- 6.6 ms (V2), against 13.9 +/- 3.2.

Claims blocked from the start¶

Claim Reason Where looked
fig1d-thalamus-photoinhibition-bias data missing The only Gad2 sessions (Ai35D x GAD2_Cre, 9 thalamic recordings) carry no photostimulus trial; there are no behaviour-only sessions.
gad2-thalamus-reduction metadata insufficient The 84 units of the Gad2 sessions match the n of Extended Data Fig. 2c, but no trial is marked as photostimulated (period 'N/A', power 0 everywhere).
muscimol-vmval-bias data missing No muscimol sessions, no infusion metadata.
wc-loss-of-excitation data missing No non-behaving recordings and no current-injection experiments with TRN photostimulation (all 36 cells are behaving; the injected current is a holding current).
indirect-pathway-too-slow data missing No whole-cell recordings of M1 neurons (every cell is in ALM). Its other onset, ALM after M1 photoinhibition, is shown under the laser onset in the whole-cell section; the claim needs both.
conduction-delay data missing No Olig3-cre x Ai32 recordings.
latency-model-t3 methods underspecified A simulation whose parameters are in the Supplementary Information, not in the text the claims were written from.
fig5-weak-photoinhibition-rates data missing No ALM session with 0.5 mW thalamus photoinhibition (VGAT ALM sessions use 10 mW only); the dandiset holds 966 of the 1214 ALM units, consistent with the Fig. 5 sessions (JRclust sorting) being absent.
fig5c-selectivity-reduced data missing Depends on fig5-weak-photoinhibition-rates.
network-models methods underspecified A modelling result specified in the Supplementary Information.
anatomy-reciprocal-thalamus data missing No histology or cell counts in the dandiset.
alm-gabaergic-no-thalamic-projection data missing No histology in the dandiset.

Changes of outcome¶

The second verification found that nine claims were given partially reproduced under criteria that have no partial clause: each says only "Reproduced when ...". The cell below counts, for each of them, the readings of the claims file that meet the whole criterion, from the tables above. Reading L of the whole-cell claims (the laser trace, question 7) is not in the claims file and is counted apart.

In [35]:

cls = {"P1": (len(alm), len(PYR["P1"]), int((alm.width_ms < 0.4).sum())),
       "P2": (len(alm), len(PYR["P2"]), int((alm.cell_type == "Narrow width spiking").sum()))}

                                               ((790, 79), (672, 67), (313, 31), (295, 30)))) for p in THP]

full["fig2f-vmval-selectivity"] = (int((f2f.counts_within_tol & (f2f.chi_ok_i | f2f.chi_ok_ii)).sum()), len(f2f))
f3f_r = f3f[f3f.units.isin(["P1", "P2"])]

full["fig6d-localized"] = (int((f6d.counts_ok & f6d.value_ok_any_Q & f6d.near_lower_than_far_Q1).sum()), len(f6d))

for claim, group, checks in (("wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization", "thalamus", [("dVm_mean", -18.7, 1.1)]),
                             ("wc-m1-small-effect", "M1", [("dVm_mean", -3.3, 1.0), ("dRate_mean", -1.4, 0.6)])):
    for reading in ("E", "M", "L"):
        r = wcp[(wcp.onset_reading == reading) & (wcp.group == group)].iloc[0]
        print(claim, reading, {q: (r[q], bool(abs(r[q] - v) <= e)) for q, v, e in checks})

    ok = [all(abs(wcp[(wcp.onset_reading == rd) & (wcp.group == group)].iloc[0][q] - v) <= e for q, v, e in checks) for rd in ("E", "M")]

    print(f"{claim}: {n_ok} of {n} readings meet the whole criterion")

No reading of the claims file meets the whole criterion of any of the nine claims. For wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization the Vm change alone is outside tolerance under E and M (and under L, which is not a reading of the claims file), so the onset, which no listed reading can judge, does not bear on the outcome; for wc-m1-small-effect the spike-rate change is outside tolerance under every onset. Partial agreement (class fractions, selective fractions, near-complete silencing, the order of the distance groups, the SNr counts under P1, the Vm change of M1 photoinhibition) is not an outcome these criteria define. The outcome of each of the nine claims was proposed to change from partially reproduced to not reproduced after the second verification; the third verification round agreed with all nine, and each is now not reproduced.

7 reproduced, 2 partially reproduced, 13 not reproduced, 17 blocked. Nine claims, whose criteria have no partial clause and which no reading meets in full, were changed from partially reproduced to not reproduced after the third verification round agreed (see Changes of outcome above).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Unit classes are run under the readings of convention C: widths computed on the deposited waveforms (P1, the Methods' rule), which are too short for the width thresholds, and the files' labels (P2), which match the paper's class sizes; for the thalamic claims of Fig. 2 and 6, all units (P3) as well. Each unit's trials are taken as those from the trial holding its first spike to the trial holding its last, as the files give no observation interval per unit, and a window that ends after a trial's stored spikes is counted as missing for that trial. Behaviour is measured in the recording sessions, not in behaviour sessions. The VM/VAL centre is the claims file's proxy (reading L2). Distances from the thalamic fibre use the files' single nominal site. The whole-cell claims are judged under the two onsets the claims file allows (E and M) and under the onset of the deposited laser trace (L), which the claims file did not know of (question 7); the outcomes are the same under M and L, nothing holds under E, and the onset latency of 7.9 ms cannot be judged under E or M, the readings the claims file lists; under L, shown pending question 7, it is 9.60 ms by V2 and 0.40 ms by V1. The (0.5, 0.5) galvo site is taken as vM1 only to show what the data give, compared with ALM at 1.5 mW.

What was found about the dataset.

  • The dandiset holds 966 of the paper's 1214 ALM units (47 of 57 sessions), 789 of 790 thalamic units and 181 of 227 SNr units (apparently only the putative GABAergic ones: 171 of the 181 by computed width, 146 by the files' label). Behaviour-only, muscimol, weak photoinhibition (Fig. 5), non-behaving and M1 whole-cell recordings and histology are absent.
  • The mean waveforms are cut short (29 to 38 samples at 25 kHz), so trough-to-peak widths longer than about 0.5 ms cannot be measured; the cell_type labels carry the classification instead, without a stated rule.
  • Spikes are stored only from the trial start to about 4.8 s after pole onset, although trials last about 9 s, so in trials with long delays the response epoch is not stored; most units hold spikes over only part of their session, with no per-unit observation interval.
  • The whole-cell trial tables leave the photostimulus columns empty; the laser time is in an OptogeneticSeries described only as 'no description'. It starts between the two delay onsets the trial times allow, 0.10 to 0.17 s after E and 0.03 to 0.10 s before M (1.40 s after pole onset in one mouse, 1.47 s in the others). One whole-cell trial table has start and stop times shifted by one row. The Vm conversion (0.001 with unit 'mV') contradicts the values, which are in mV.
  • Every electrode group, in thalamus and SNr too, carries the ALM coordinates; the SNr units of one mouse are at AP -1.56 mm; there is no VM/VAL location label; unit_y has no stated reference, so whether it is depth below the pia is not said. Session start times are the date of conversion (all on 2017-06-27), not of recording, so the missing ALM sessions cannot be identified by date.
  • The Gad2 sessions (genotype given as Ai35D x GAD2_Cre, an Arch line, where the paper used Gad2-IRES-Cre with ChR2 in TRN) carry no photostimulus trial, though their 84 units match the optrode units of Extended Data Fig. 2c. The VGAT thalamic sessions give 2.23 mW where the paper gives 10 mW. PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions with thalamic photostimulation at 10 to 45 mW and C57BL6 thalamic sessions are not described in the paper; the (0.5, 0.5) photostimulation site is not named.
